_comment: Per-provider allowances for backend/serp/quota.py. Task 23, descoped:
DECISIONS.md 'EXP -- Build task 23, sharply descoped' keeps the quota
ledger and cuts six of the eight adapters, so only the two that survive
have rows here.
THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE NOT THE AUTHORITY AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE.
They are seeded from docs/tasks/refactor/ADDENDUM-google-jobs-providers.md
section 2, whose own note says several entries are reported secondhand,
and 23-serp-abstraction.md says to verify each against the provider on
first integration. quota.Ledger asks the PROVIDER how much is left and
treats these as a description, because the reason this file exists at all
is a measurement in the other direction: DECISIONS.md, 'EXP -- The repo's
own SerpApi ledger undercounts real spend by 3.3x'. google_jobs_query_stats
implied 41 searches used this month; the SerpApi account itself read 137.
A ledger that counts rows this pipeline remembered to write is a memory of
intentions, and its first symptom is a month that goes dark early with no
error anywhere.
WHY THE UNITS DIFFER AND ARE NOT CONVERTED. SerpApi bills one search per
call against a monthly search allowance. Apify bills per RESULT out of a
dollar balance, so a 10-result query costs ten times a 1-result one and
its account endpoint answers in USD. Converting would need a per-result
price that is a property of the actor and the plan, so reconcilable=false
says the comparison is not available rather than inventing a rate. This is
D37 from the other end.
REJECTED: a `daily_budget` here. config/google-queries.json already carries
per-bucket daily budgets for the nightly bank, and a second daily number in
a second file would be two schedulers disagreeing. This file answers 'how
much does the account hold', never 'how much may tonight use'.

_reserve_comment: Searches held back from this pipeline. 0 = no reserve, which is the
honest default: picking a number here is a policy call the owner has
not made, and D71 is the standing example of what filing an invented
ceiling looks like. It is not decoration -- THREE other things spend
running the nightly bank. Set it if the month starts going dark early.
serpapi._verified: not verified against the vendor; seeded from ADDENDUM section 2

_allowance_comment: null, deliberately, and NOT 50. The addendum's '~50 equivalent' is $5
divided by ~$0.01/job divided by 10 jobs per query -- a derived
estimate of QUERIES from a dollar balance, and writing it here as an
allowance in `results` would be a third unit pretending to be the
second. The account endpoint answers in USD; that is what reconcile()
reports and it is reported as USD.
